findings.description: The inline policy grants full wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the deploy user unrestricted control over compute, storage, serverless and monitoring resources across the account. ec2:* and lambda:* in particular enable privilege escalation (e.g. passing/assuming roles via instance or function creation) and s3:* permits reading or deleting all bucket data.

A permanent IAM access key is created for the service user and its secret is stored in Terraform state in plaintext (no pgp_key is configured, so encrypted_secret will be empty and the cleartext secret lands in state). Long-lived static keys with no rotation attached to an admin-like policy are a high-value credential-theft target.

The access key material is exposed as a root module output without sensitive = true, so it is printed to the console and CI logs on every apply and stored unmasked in state/plan artifacts. Because no pgp_key was supplied to the access key resource, encrypted_secret is unencrypted/empty and the underlying secret is retrievable from state.

A long-lived IAM user with force_destroy = true is used for deployment automation rather than an assumable role with temporary credentials; force_destroy also allows silent deletion of attached keys and login profiles, undermining credential accountability.
